# Highlight Open Files

<!-- Generated by Copilot -->

A VS Code extension that highlights currently open files in the editor tabs and file explorer with a configurable color and badge.

> **Based on [highlight-files](https://github.com/ArturoDent/highlight-files) by [Arturo Dent](https://github.com/ArturoDent).** This fork changes the behavior to highlight all open files (instead of only non-workspace files) and renames the extension accordingly.

## Features

- Adds a colored label to tabs and explorer entries of all currently open files
- Adds a configurable badge (1-2 characters, including unicode) to open file tabs
- Color and badges update in real-time as you open and close files
- Fully configurable via VS Code settings

## Settings

| Setting                                            | Type      | Default | Description                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.color`      | `boolean` | `true`  | Enable colored labels on tabs of open files     |
| `highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.badges`     | `boolean` | `true`  | Enable badges on tabs of open files             |
| `highlightOpenFiles.decorations.badge`             | `string`  | `●`     | Badge character (1-2 chars, supports unicode)   |
| `highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.activeFile` | `boolean` | `true`  | Enable distinct color/badge for the active file |
| `highlightOpenFiles.decorations.activeBadge`       | `string`  | `▶`     | Badge character for the active file (1-2 chars) |
| `highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.propagate`  | `boolean` | `false` | Propagate color to parent folders in explorer   |

## Active File Highlighting

When `highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.activeFile` is enabled, the currently focused file receives a distinct color and badge — making it easy to spot in the explorer and tab bar at a glance.

The active file uses the `highlightOpenFiles.activeFile` color token (defaults to bright purple `#c586c0` on dark themes). Customize both colors independently:

```jsonc
"workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "highlightOpenFiles.openFiles":  "#7a4eb580",  // open files — muted, 50% opacity
    "highlightOpenFiles.activeFile": "#c586c0"      // active file — brighter, full opacity
}
```

The active badge defaults to `▶`. Change it in settings:

```jsonc
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.activeBadge": "★"
```

To disable just the active file distinction while keeping open file highlights, set `highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.activeFile` to `false`.

## Color Customization

The extension contributes a theme color `highlightOpenFiles.openFiles` which defaults to [rebeccapurple](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#valdef-color-rebeccapurple) (`#663399`). This color was added to the CSS standard in 2014 in memory of Rebecca Meyer, the six-year-old daughter of web standards pioneer [Eric A. Meyer](https://meyerweb.com/), who passed away from brain cancer. The CSS community honored her by naming the color after her — making it the only CSS named color dedicated to a real person. You can customize it in your `settings.json`:

```jsonc
"workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "highlightOpenFiles.openFiles": "#7a4eb5"  // any hex color, supports opacity e.g. #7a4eb580
}
```

### Color Examples

| Style                     | Hex         | Description                       |
| ------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| Rebeccapurple (default)   | `#663399`   | Soft purple, works in both themes |
| Soft green                | `#57c957`   | Gentler on light themes           |
| Orange                    | `#ff8c00`   | Warm, visible in dark themes      |
| Sky blue                  | `#4ec9e0`   | Calm, works in both themes        |
| Purple                    | `#c586c0`   | Subtle, blends with many themes   |
| Red                       | `#f44747`   | High urgency feel                 |
| Dimmed (50% opacity)      | `#91ff0080` | Subtle overlay, non-distracting   |
| Very dimmed (30% opacity) | `#91ff004d` | Minimal, barely-there highlight   |

The last two hex digits control **opacity**: `ff` = fully opaque, `80` = 50%, `4d` = 30%.

### Badge Examples

> **Note:** The badge value must be the **actual character** — paste it directly into `settings.json` or the Settings UI. Unicode escape sequences like `\u2B24` are **not** supported in VS Code settings JSON.

```jsonc
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.badge": "⬤"     // ✅ paste the character directly
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.badge": "\u2B24" // ❌ does not work
```

VS Code settings are plain JSON strings — the JSON spec does allow `\uXXXX` escapes, but the VS Code settings engine reads the value as a literal string after parsing. This means `\u2B24` arrives as the six characters `\`, `u`, `2`, `B`, `2`, `4` rather than the single character `⬤`, and the badge will display those raw characters or be rejected by the 2-character length limit. Always paste the actual unicode character instead.

You can browse and copy unicode characters at [symbl.cc](https://symbl.cc) or [unicode.org](https://www.unicode.org/charts/).

| Badge | Copy this | Description                         |
| ----- | --------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `!`   | `!`       | Default — simple exclamation mark   |
| `⬤`   | `⬤`       | Filled circle — clean dot indicator |
| `●`   | `●`       | Medium filled circle                |
| `◆`   | `◆`       | Filled diamond                      |
| `★`   | `★`       | Star                                |
| `▶`   | `▶`       | Right-pointing triangle             |
| `»`   | `»`       | Double angle — subtle marker        |
| `✦`   | `✦`       | Four-pointed star                   |

## Preset Examples

Copy any preset into your `settings.json` to get started quickly.

### Preset A — Classic (default)
Color + badge, muted open files, bright active file:
```jsonc
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.badge": "●",
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.activeBadge": "▶",
"workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "highlightOpenFiles.openFiles":  "#7a4eb580",  // muted purple, 50% opacity
    "highlightOpenFiles.activeFile": "#c586c0"      // bright pink-purple, full opacity
}
```

### Preset B — Badge only (SCM-friendly)
No color, so git decorations are unaffected:
```jsonc
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.color": false,
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.badge": "○",
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.activeBadge": "◉"
```

### Preset C — Folder awareness
Propagates color up to parent folders so you can see which folders have open files:
```jsonc
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.propagate": true,
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.badge": "◆",
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.activeBadge": "★",
"workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "highlightOpenFiles.openFiles":  "#4ec9e080",  // cyan, 50% opacity
    "highlightOpenFiles.activeFile": "#ffcc00"      // yellow — visually distinct
}
```

### Preset D — Minimal (active file only)
Only the currently focused file is highlighted, nothing else:
```jsonc
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.badges": false,
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.color": false,
"highlightOpenFiles.decorations.enable.activeFile": true,
"workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "highlightOpenFiles.activeFile": "#ffcc00"
}
```

## Prerequisites

These built-in VS Code settings control whether any file decoration provider can show colors and badges. They default to `true`, so you typically don't need to change them — but if decorations are not showing, verify they are enabled:

**Editor tabs:**
```jsonc
"workbench.editor.decorations.badges": true,
"workbench.editor.decorations.colors": true
```

**File explorer:**
```jsonc
"explorer.decorations.badges": true,
"explorer.decorations.colors": true
```

> **Note:** The `Problems > Decorations: Enabled` setting takes precedence — if a file has problems, it will be colored by the Problems decorator instead of this extension.

## Known Issues

- **SCM badge conflict:** The badge slot is shared with other decoration providers (e.g. git SCM). If a file has git status, the SCM badge (`M`, `U`, `D`) takes precedence over this extension's badge. Use Preset B (badge only, no color) or disable badges via `enable.badges: false` if you rely on SCM badges.
- After installing, you may need to reload VS Code once to activate the extension.
